claim: Coolify officially supports Debian-based (Debian, Ubuntu - all versions, non-LTS Ubuntu requires manual install), Redhat, SUSE, Arch, Alpine and Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit; other distros may work but are untested, and the docs explicitly recommend a fresh server to avoid conflicts with existing applications.
quote: It's best to use a fresh server for Coolify to avoid any conflicts with existing applications. ... Docker installed via snap is not supported!

claim: The Coolify install script installs essential tools (curl, wget, git, jq, openssl), installs Docker Engine 24+, configures Docker daemon/logging settings, creates /data/coolify, configures SSH keys for server management, and starts Coolify; minimum spec is 2 CPU cores, 2GB RAM, 30GB storage.
quote: Installs essential tools (curl, wget, git, jq, openssl) ... Installs Docker Engine (version 24+) ... Configures Docker settings (logging, daemon) ... Sets up directories at /data/coolify ... Configures SSH keys for server management

claim: Coolify has hardcoded port-80 validation: coolify-proxy fails to (re)start from the web UI with 'Port 80 is in use' even when the proxy is reconfigured to custom ports like 5080/5443, making coexistence with an existing reverse proxy on port 80 a known friction point (repo ~56.6k stars).
quote: Port 80 is in use. You must stop the process using this port.

claim: The official/recommended way to move Coolify's dashboard off the default port 8000 is an upgrade-safe docker-compose.override.yml in /data/coolify/source/ (or setting APP_PORT in .env), keeping the container port at 80; ports 80/443 must remain free for the Caddy/Traefik proxy if using HTTPS custom domains.
quote: create a docker-compose.override.yml file in /data/coolify/source/. This method is 'upgrade-safe' ... Keep the container port at 80 (only change the host port) ... Ports 80 and 443 must remain available if using HTTPS with custom domains.

claim: Docker (and thus Coolify) breaks in an unprivileged Proxmox LXC because runc 1.2+ writes net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0 which the mapped root cannot do without CAP_NET_ADMIN, and the AppArmor profile probe reads host-root-owned /sys paths; the working config is a privileged LXC with features nesting=1,keyctl=1,fuse=1, lxc.apparmor.profile: unconfined and an empty lxc.cap.drop.
quote: runc 1.2+ unconditionally writes to net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0 ... the mapped root lacks the necessary CAP_NET_ADMIN capability ... features: nesting=1,keyctl=1,fuse=1 / lxc.apparmor.profile: unconfined / lxc.cap.drop:

claim: For production Docker workloads on Proxmox the 2026 verdict is to use a KVM VM rather than Docker-in-LXC: VMs give full kernel isolation, live migration and 'standard Docker, no hacks', whereas Docker-in-LXC is 'the worst of both worlds' with fragile workarounds, costing only ~256-512MB extra RAM.
quote: VM + Docker is the production choice ... 'standard Docker, no hacks' ... Docker-in-LXC as combining 'the worst of both worlds' with 'fragile workarounds'

claim: A community guide runs Coolify successfully in a privileged Proxmox LXC with the nesting feature enabled, chosen for being lightweight and easy to migrate around a cluster, with the main friction being networking (single-IP hosts needing Cloudflare tunnels).
quote: uncheck unprivileged container ... go under options to enable the nesting feature flag which will enable nested virtualization ... running coolify in an LXC makes it easy for me to move it around my proxmox cluster, and also its very light weight
